subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Miller–Urey experiment provided evidence that:
options: Organic molecules can form from inorganic precursors under early-Earth conditions
Cells arise only from pre-existing cells
Oxygen was abundant on early Earth
questions.explain: Passing sparks through a reducing gas mixture produced amino acids, supporting abiotic synthesis of organic molecules.

questions.q: The 'RNA world' hypothesis is attractive because RNA can:
options: Both store information and catalyse reactions
questions.explain: Ribozymes show RNA can act as both a heritable information store and a catalyst, so it could precede DNA and protein enzymes.

questions.q: LUCA refers to the:
questions.explain: LUCA is the inferred common ancestor from which all current cellular life descends.

questions.q: The spontaneous formation of phospholipid vesicles was an important step in the origin of cells because it provided:
options: A membrane-bound compartment separating internal chemistry from the environment
questions.explain: Enclosing reactions within a bilayer allowed concentration gradients and protected early self-replicating molecules.

questions.q: A defining feature of eukaryotic cells not found in prokaryotes is:
questions.explain: Eukaryotes compartmentalise functions in membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes lack these.

questions.q: The organelle that carries out aerobic respiration and produces most ATP is the:
questions.explain: Mitochondria host the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, generating ATP aerobically.

questions.q: Rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with ribosomes and functions mainly in:
questions.explain: Ribosomes on the rough ER synthesise proteins that are then processed and transported.

questions.q: As a cell increases in size, its surface area to volume ratio:
options: Decreases, limiting the rate of exchange with the environment
questions.explain: Volume rises faster than surface area, so large cells struggle to exchange materials fast enough — a key constraint on cell size.

questions.q: Which structure is present in a plant cell but absent from a typical animal cell?
questions.explain: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall (and often chloroplasts and a large central vacuole) not found in animal cells.

questions.q: The resolution of a microscope is its ability to:
options: Distinguish two close points as separate
questions.explain: Resolution is about clarity/detail; magnification only enlarges the image. Electron microscopes have far higher resolution than light microscopes.

questions.q: Mature mammalian red blood cells lack a nucleus and mitochondria. This is best interpreted as:
options: Specialisation that maximises space for haemoglobin and oxygen transport
questions.explain: Loss of the nucleus creates room for haemoglobin; such atypical cells show that cell structure relates to function.

questions.q: The fluid interior of a cell in which organelles are suspended and many reactions occur is the:
questions.explain: The cytoplasm (cytosol plus organelles) is the site of many metabolic reactions such as glycolysis.

questions.q: Which list correctly matches an organelle to its function?
options: Golgi apparatus – modifies and packages proteins
questions.explain: The Golgi modifies, sorts and packages proteins/lipids into vesicles for secretion or use in the cell.

questions.q: Viruses are not classified as living cells mainly because they:
options: Lack cytoplasm and metabolism and cannot reproduce independently
questions.explain: Viruses are acellular, non-metabolising, and are obligate intracellular parasites that require a host cell to replicate.

questions.q: The protein coat that encloses a virus's genetic material is called the:
questions.explain: The capsid is a protein coat; some viruses also have a lipid envelope derived from host membranes.

questions.q: Viral genomes may be composed of:
questions.explain: Viruses show great diversity: their genetic material can be single- or double-stranded DNA or RNA.

questions.q: In the lytic cycle of a bacteriophage, the host cell:
options: Is destroyed as new virus particles are released
Integrates the viral genome and survives
questions.explain: In the lytic cycle the virus replicates and lyses (bursts) the host to release progeny virions.

questions.q: In the lysogenic cycle, viral DNA:
options: Integrates into the host genome and is copied when the host divides
questions.explain: The integrated prophage is replicated along with the host DNA and may later switch to the lytic cycle.

questions.q: The very high mutation rate of many RNA viruses helps explain why:
options: New variants and vaccine escape can arise rapidly
questions.explain: Error-prone RNA replication generates variation quickly, driving antigenic change (e.g. influenza, SARS-CoV-2).

questions.q: A student calculates magnification as image size ÷ actual size. If an image is 50 mm across and magnification is ×500, the actual size is:
questions.explain: Actual size = 50 mm ÷ 500 = 0.1 mm = 100 µm.
